title: 맥베스
prompt:
INPUT: the attached image is the approved character; keep her.

CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — the personification of «맥베스» (tragedy). Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut, skin tone and body proportions; expression and hair motion may change.

STYLE: 섬세한 선화 + 회화적 채색의 성인 판타지 삽화풍

SYMBOL (this one only, as an accessory or an object in the scene — never printed on or woven into the clothes): "움직이는 버넘 숲".

AGE: keep her age as in the attached image; add no wrinkles, folds or under-eye shadows, even when she smiles.

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her in the outfit chosen in SCENE; her book shows only through accessories and objects around her — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never her form costume, never a carried book. Everything else follows SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; COMPOSITION in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

SETTING: a stylised stage, editorial or fantasy set, not bound to a real year — still one real adult woman in a believable space, no creatures.

SCENE (chosen):
Place: an old stone chapel lit by candles
Outfit: a 1920s bias-cut satin lounge gown
POSTURE: perched on a ledge or edge.
SUPPORT: she sits on the edge, her weight on her hips.
COMPOSITION: a three-quarter shot from her head to just above the knees; body facing the camera; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
BOTH HANDS: both hands brace on the edge on either side of her hips.
LEGS: knees together, feet slightly apart.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: level lowered brow, steady unblinking eyes, mouth closed in a straight line, jaw set.
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — more scene-appropriate shoulder, back, midriff or leg exposure; cover chest and pelvis
action_level: mostly posed — a paused or held moment of the selected activity
source_influence: balanced — her book shows as one accessory and one object in the scene; the outfit keeps its own colours and patterns
separates_preference: strongly prefer separates — use separate top and bottom by default; a garment named in the chosen Outfit takes priority

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face, hair and body — not its garment, layers, sash, tassels, jewelry, hair ornaments or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; that outfit must read at first glance, keeping its own recognisable colours and parts. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her book belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her own costume, genre or palette.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. Where the place is busy, other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her and never a character from her book. No text, no lettering, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border; pages and spines stay unlettered.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, about 7.5 heads tall — height from the legs, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may stay outside the crop, and fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.
